title: Recording, tape copying: Don’t Let It Bring You Down, Café On The Left Bank, I’m Carrying, Deliver Your Children, I’ve Had Enough, With A Little Luck by Wings | 1977
content:
Fair Carol, St John, US Virgin Islands
Producer: Paul McCartney
Engineers: Geoff Emerick, Mark Vigars

Wings began recording the London Town song ‘Don’t Let It Bring You Down’ on 24 May 1977.

The session took place on board the Fair Carol, a 105-foot yacht kitted out with studio equipment from the Record Plant in New York. It was moored in Waterlemon Bay, St John, in the US Virgin Islands, where Wings were recording the album.

A demo of ‘Don’t Let It Bring You Down’ had been recorded by Paul McCartney earlier in the year. He played the recording to two visitors to the sessions, journalist Paul Gambaccini and photographer Henry Diltz. McCartney then picked up an acoustic guitar and began performing the song, during which he was joined by Denny Laine.

Wings then began working up the song in earnest. McCartney switch to bass guitar, Jimmy McCulloch joined on second guitar, and Joe English was on drums. Work on the song continued the following day.

Geoff Emerick also made copies of some of the master recordings made to date during Wings’ time in the Caribbean: ‘Cafe On The Left Bank’, ‘I’m Carrying’, Denny Laine’s ‘Find A Way Somehow’, ‘Deliver Your Children’, ‘I’ve Had Enough’, and ‘With A Little Luck’.
